work.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra
work.notes: Nietzsche's philosophical-literary work, first issued in parts from 1883 to 1885. Preserve its dramatic voices, imagery, and irony rather than treating every speech as a flat doctrinal statement.

edition.label: Thomas Common translation; Project Gutenberg #1998

passages.citationLabel: Thus Spake Zarathustra, Part I, “The Three Metamorphoses,” Common trans.
passages.translationText: Three metamorphoses of the spirit do I designate to you: how the spirit becometh a camel, the camel a lion, and the lion at last a child.
passages.interpretiveNote: The camel, lion, and child form a staged image of bearing inherited burdens, winning freedom from imposed values, and attaining an affirmative capacity to create. It is a literary-philosophical image, not a literal psychology taxonomy.
passages.period: 1883–1885 mature literary philosophy; historical English translation
